title: Free to Interacting Map for Crystalline SPT Phases: Equivariance vs Crystalline Equivalence
abstract: Freed and Hopkins developed an ansatz for classifying interacting SPT phases using invertible field theories with a natural Free to Interacting (FTI) map from free fermion phases. This ansatz has been generalized to include crystalline phases and a crystalline equivalence principle (CEP). However, motivated by failure of the CEP for weak free fermions and the FTI, here we generalize the original Freed and Hopkins ansatz to a fully equivariant version for symmorphic crystallographic symmetries and show there is a natural equivariant FTI map from symmorphic crystalline weak free fermions. We further discuss why this equivariant ansatz is both mathematically and physically more natural than the spatial symmetry extension by Freed and Hopkins and why full equivariance should hold over the CEP.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a rigorous framework to classify interacting Symmetry Protected Topological (SPT) phases in crystalline systems. It proposes an equivariant Free to Interacting (FTI) map that corrects previous classification schemes by prioritizing full crystallographic equivariance over the established Crystalline Equivalence Principle. This advances our understanding of topological order in materials with crystal symmetries.
main_problem: The paper addresses developing a natural classification scheme for interacting Symmetry Protected Topological (SPT) phases, specifically resolving the conflict between established crystalline equivalence principles and results derived from free fermions.
main_result: The authors propose a fully equivariant Free to Interacting (FTI) map that respects full crystallographic equivariance, arguing this structure is more natural than previous constructions based on the potentially flawed Crystalline Equivalence Principle (CEP).
method: The work employs advanced algebraic topology tools, including equivariant K-theory and Anderson duality, to construct and analyze a candidate FTI map connecting free fermion theories to interacting SPT phases.
model_or_system: The focus is on crystalline SPT phases characterized by an internal symmetry group H and a crystallographic symmetry group G. The analysis compares classifications derived from invertible field theories against those arising from weak free fermions.
key_observables: Classification invariants such as $\pi_0(	ext{Sd}(H))$ for interacting phases, and $KO^{d+s-2}_P(T^d)$ for free fermions; the kernel and cokernel of the proposed FTI map are key diagnostics.
important_parameters: The dimensionality ($d$), internal symmetry structure ($H$), and crystallographic point group action ($P$) are central parameters governing the classification.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that full equivariance with respect to the spatial symmetry group $P$ should take precedence over maintaining the Crystalline Equivalence Principle (CEP).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first identifying the failure of the CEP for free fermions, then generalizing the Freed and Hopkins ansatz to a fully equivariant version, and finally constructing and analyzing the resulting natural equivariant FTI map.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical machinery (equivariant K-theory) to classify topological phases in crystalline materials, which is crucial for understanding symmetry protection beyond simple lattice models relevant to AMO physics.
